name: Makada
description: Photo-informed three-servo wire-leg hexapod with a rear-mounted NodeMCU 1.0 ESP-12E and separate regulated servo rail. Dimensions and mounting are estimates; native CAD and commanded gait preview.

metadata.note: Upright landscape rear mount parallel to the servo backs; placement and mounting remain estimates.
metadata.dimensionSource: upstream ESP12E_DEVKIT.lbr 25.4 x 48.26 mm outline, 22.86 mm header rows; placement estimated

metadata.note: Illustrative separate external BEC distribution connector; regulated servo 5 V and shared ground. No servo load from NodeMCU 3V3 or VIN.

motion.name: Forward eight-phase gait
motion.description: Firmware phase order with three coupled servo outputs. Side front/hind wire pairs sweep about vertical shafts; middle pair tilts about the horizontal center shaft. Pulse-to-angle mapping and dimensions are estimates; no measured feedback.

hardware.name: Makada TCP adapter
hardware.description: Project-owned Python broker serializes authenticated commands, telemetry, heartbeat and STOP on one connection. Credentials remain local.

capabilities.label: Inspect hardware
capabilities.description: Read pin map and saved calibration offline.

capabilities.label: Preview gait
capabilities.description: Offline commanded pulse sequence from the saved profile; not live measurements.

capabilities.label: Connect and monitor
capabilities.description: Hold the single real TCP connection with live heartbeat. Cancellation sends STOP.

capabilities.label: Read status and stop outputs
capabilities.description: Authenticate and read real STATUS/DIAG, then send STOP and detach all servo outputs before disconnecting. Requires physical-operation authorization and robot support.

capabilities.label: Walk forward
capabilities.description: Move the real robot forward over Wi-Fi. Requests of 1–100 gait cycles run in verified batches of up to 20; any timeout stops the remaining plan. A cycle is not a measured distance.

steps.title: Gait cycles
steps.description: 1–100 cycles. Larger requests use verified batches; no automatic retry.
